A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M3HF research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Overcooked training results, feedback-quality experiments and component and feedback-phase ablations in Figures 3–4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds an IRAT comparison in Table 3 and Google Research Football results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, agent-specific feedback parsing, reward templates, reward pools and weight-update rules are retained. The revised rollout estimator and robustness arguments change performance evaluation and theoretical justification; they do not establish a different reward-learning algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only Overcooked layouts A–C with two salad recipes. v3 additionally evaluates Google Research Football 5v5 against HARD built-in opponents, introducing a substantially different domain, action space and coordination task. The corrected B/C descriptions in Figure 2 do not introduce new Overcooked layouts.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds IRAT with three handcrafted reward variants to the Overcooked comparison. Existing IPPO, MAPPO and macro-action comparisons remain. Football plots identify IPPO and MAPPO; although their caption also names MACCS, no corresponding plotted series verifies its participation.

E3.justification: Football introduces 100 training iterations, 8,000 episodes of 3,000 steps, six plotted metrics and 60-second feedback rollouts. Section 4 also replaces the stated millions of steps per iteration with an episodic hierarchy, specified in Section 5 as 25 episodes of up to 200 steps per iteration. Retained Overcooked budgets remain 1,000 iterations and 25,000 episodes; these revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The new third ablation compares three IRAT reward designs with progressively different coordination requirements, adding analysis of dependence on handcrafted shaping. The parsing/weight-adjustment and single-versus-multiple-feedback ablations already appeared in v1 Appendix D and retain their results when moved into v3 Section 5.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated statistical estimator from a single-rollout time average to an average of discounted returns over X independent rollouts, with a new i.i.d. assumption. Experimental reporting otherwise retains three-seed means and standard deviations, including the new IRAT table; no increase in training runs or new significance testing is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds IRAT results at four checkpoints and six Football performance curves. Table 3 newly reports M3HF at 164.8 ± 1.2 and IRAT-rw_1 at 68.9 ± 10.1 at iteration 400. Figures 3–4 and Tables 1–2 retain their earlier results, including M3HF's 102.7 ± 10.8 ablation return. The new Table 3 score is not reconciled with the retained Overcooked-B curve, so it cannot establish a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1 replaces the ergodic time-average/discounted-occupancy argument with independent discounted-rollout estimation and adds Assumption A.4. Proposition 4.2 replaces a zero-mean-noise expectation bound allowing loss proportional to the generation count with an arbitrary-feedback guarantee accumulating beneficial increments and allowing only a constant loss. The proofs are substantially replaced, including new Lemma B.1 in v3 Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: MHF-MG, LLM-mediated multi-phase feedback, adaptive reward weighting, robustness and improved multi-agent learning. Additional experiments and revised theoretical statements do not materially rewrite these headline contributions.

C2.justification: The robustness interpretation changes from limited expected degradation under zero-mean noise to accumulating helpful feedback with only a single bounded degradation under arbitrary feedback. v3 also adds explanations involving reduced policy interference for IPPO, coordination failures under fixed IRAT rewards, and feedback-induced off-ball movement in Football. The original VLM limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the parser as gpt-4o-2024-11-20, discloses baseline hyperparameter-search ranges and validation-based selection, and clarifies policy sharing. Football captions provide observation/action specifications, environment configuration and feedback-video duration. Existing Overcooked prompts, hardware descriptions and selected hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: Related work gains substantive positioning against PbMARL's offline preference setting and MOTIF's single-agent intrinsic rewards, plus a discussion of difficulties extending EUREKA to multiple agents. Additional language-feedback, theoretical and Football references broaden the research context. Publication-year and venue updates for retained works are bibliographic changes rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: The rollout and robustness sections and their proofs are substantially rewritten, related-work passages are expanded and restructured, and existing ablations move from an appendix into the main experimental narrative. Appendices are reorganized, and acknowledgments and publication information are added.

P2.justification: v3 revises the workflow diagram, corrects Figure 2's B/C caption descriptions, relocates and compresses the existing ablation tables, and moves Algorithm 1 within the appendix. It adds the IRAT results table and two Football figures containing environment/configuration displays and six performance panels. Existing Overcooked plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens empirical coverage, adds useful comparator and implementation information, and improves the discount-aware rollout argument. However, its stronger robustness proof assumes intervening losses disappear at positive milestones without establishing this from the algorithm (Appendix B). Table 3's new M3HF score is also unreconciled with the retained curve for the same labeled task. These substantive validity concerns counterbalance the additions, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
